edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: PAX ecce, dilectissimi fratres, Ecclesiae reddita est et, quod difficile nuper incredulis ac perfidis impossibile videbatur, ope atque ultione divina securitas nostra reparata est. In laetitiam mentes redeunt, et, tempestate pressurae ac nube discussa, tranquillitas ac serenitas refulserunt. Dandae laudes Deo, et beneficia ejus ac munera cum gratiarum actione celebranda, quamvis agere gratias nostra vox nec in persecutione cessaverit. Neque enim tantum inimico licere potest ut non, qui Dominum toto corde et anima et virtute diligimus, benedictiones ejus et laudes semper et ubique cum gloria praedicemus. Exoptatus votis omnium dies venit, et, post longae noctis horribilem tetramque caliginem, Domini luce radiatus mundus eluxit. Confessores, praeconio boni nominis claros et virtutis ac fidei laudibus gloriosos, laetis conspectibus intuemur, sanctis osculis adhaerentes, desideratos diu inexplebili cupiditate complectimur. Adest militum Christi cohors candida, qui persecutionis urgentus ferociam turbulentam stabili congressione fregerunt, parati ad patientiam carceris, armati ad tolerantiam mortis. Repugnastis fortiter saeculo, spectaculum gloriosum praebuistis Deo, secuturis fratribus fuistis exemplo. Religiosa vox Christum locuta est, in quem se semel credidisse confessa est. Illustres manus, quae non nisi divinis operibus assueverant, sacrificiis sacrilegis restiterunt. Sanctificata ora coelestibus cibis, post corpus et sanguinem Domini, profana contagia et idolorum reliquias respuerunt. Ab impio sceleratoque velamine, quo illic velabantur sacrificantium capita captiva, caput vestrum liberum mansit. Frons cum signo Dei pura, diaboli coronam ferre non potuit, coronae se Domini reservavit. Quam vos laete sinu suo excipit mater Ecclesia de praelio revertentes! quam beata, quam gaudens portas suas aperit, ut adunatis agminibus intretis, de hoste prostrato trophaea referentes! Cum triumphantibus viris et feminae veniunt, quae cum saeculo dimicantes, sexum quoque vicerunt. Veniunt et geminata militiae suae gloria virgines, et pueri annos suos virtutibus transeuntes. Necnon et caetera stantium multitudo vestram gloriam sequitur, proximis et pene conjunctis laudis insignibus vestigia vestra comitatur. Eadem et in illis sinceritas cordis, eadem fidei tenacis integritas. Inconcussis praeceptorum coelestium radicibus nixos et evangelicis traditionibus roboratos, non praescripta exilia, non destinata tormenta, non rei familiaris damna, non corporis supplicia terruerunt. Explorandae fidei praefiniebantur dies. Sed qui saeculo renuntiasse se meminit, nullum saeculi diem novit; nec tempora terrena jam computat qui aeternitatem de Deo sperat. Nemo, fratres dilectissimi, nemo hanc gloriam mutilet, nemo incorruptam stantium firmitatem maligna obtrectatione debilitet. Cum dies negantibus praestitutus excessit, quisquis professus intra diem non est, Christianum se esse confessus est. Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum Dominum confiteri: secundus ad gloriam gradus est cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judice conscientiam puram cordis integritate custodit. Illic, fortitudo promptior, hic sollicitudo securior. Ille appropinquante hora sua, jam maturus inventus est; hic fortasse dilatus est qui, patrimonio derelicto, idcirco secessit quia non erat negaturus: confiteretur utique si fuisset et ipse detentus.
pass_a_gloss: Behold, most beloved brothers, peace has been restored to the Church, and what recently seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless, our security has been repaired by divine aid and vengeance. Minds return to joy, and with the storm of oppression and cloud dispersed, tranquility and serenity have shone forth. Praises must be given to God, and His benefits and gifts must be celebrated with thanksgiving, although our voice did not cease to give thanks even in persecution. For not even the enemy can be allowed so much that we, who love the Lord with our whole heart and soul and strength, do not always and everywhere proclaim His blessings and praises with glory. The day longed for by all has come, and after the horrible and dark night, the world has shone forth radiant with the Lord's light. We gaze upon the confessors, renowned for their good name and glorious for the praises of virtue and faith, with joyful sights, clinging to them with holy kisses, embracing those long desired with insatiable longing. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers is present, who broke the fierce and turbulent fury of persecution with a stable confrontation, prepared for the patience of prison, armed for the endurance of death. You resisted the world strongly, you presented a glorious spectacle to God, you were an example to subsequent brothers. The religious voice spoke Christ, in whom it confessed to have once believed. Illustrious hands, which were accustomed only to divine works, resisted sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly foods, after the body and blood of the Lord, rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your head remained free from the impious and wicked veil, with which the heads of those sacrificing were captive. Your forehead, pure with the sign of God, could not bear the devil's crown, it reserved itself for the Lord's crown. How gladly the mother Church receives you, returning from battle! How blessed, how rejoicing she opens her gates, so that you may enter with gathered troops, bringing back trophies from the prostrate enemy! With the triumphant men, women also come, who, fighting with the world, also overcame their sex. The virgins also come, with the double glory of their military service, and the boys, who surpassed their years with virtues. And also the rest of the multitude of those standing follows your glory, accompanying your footsteps with the closest and almost connected badges of praise. The same sincerity of heart is in them, the same tenacity of faith. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by evangelical traditions, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, nor destined torments, nor losses of family, nor bodily punishments. Days were set apart for testing faith. But he who remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world; nor does he who hopes for eternity from God now compute earthly times. No one, most beloved brothers, no one should mutilate this glory, no one should weaken the uncorrupted firmness of those standing with malignant detraction. When the day set apart for those denying has passed, whoever has not professed within the day has confessed himself to be a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord, apprehended by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step to glory is to be reserved for the Lord by a cautious withdrawal. That is a public confession, this is a private one. The former overcomes the judge of the world, the latter, content with his own judge, God, keeps a pure conscience with the integrity of heart. There, fortitude is more prompt, here solicitude is more secure. The former, with his hour approaching, was already found mature; the latter, perhaps delayed, who, having abandoned his patrimony, withdrew for that reason, because he was not going to deny: he would certainly have confessed if he had also been detained.

pass_b_english: My beloved brothers, peace has returned to the Church, and what recently seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless has come to pass: our security has been restored through God's help and his vengeance. Joy has returned to our minds; the storm of oppression has blown over and the cloud has lifted, so that tranquility and serenity shine forth once more. We must give praise to God and celebrate his benefits and gifts with thanksgiving, even though our voice never stopped giving thanks, not even during the persecution. After all, the enemy cannot be allowed so much power that we who love the Lord with our whole heart and soul and strength would fail to proclaim his blessings and praises everywhere and always, with glory.

The day everyone longed for has arrived. After the horrible, dark gloom of a long night, the world has blazed with the Lord's light. We gaze on the confessors, famous for their good name and glorious for the praise of their virtue and faith. With joyful hearts we cling to them with holy kisses, embracing those we have desired for so long with a longing that could never be satisfied. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers stands here — men who broke the fierce and turbulent fury of the persecution by standing their ground, ready for the patience prison demands, armed for the endurance death demands. You resisted the world with strength. You gave God a glorious spectacle. You became an example for the brothers who would follow.

A religious voice spoke Christ, confessing that it had believed in him once and for all. Illustrious hands, accustomed only to divine works, refused to take part in sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly food, after receiving the body and blood of the Lord, spat out profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your heads remained free of the impious, wicked veil that covered the captive heads of those who sacrificed. Your foreheads, marked pure with the sign of God, could not bear the devil's crown; they reserved themselves for the Lord's crown. How gladly mother Church welcomes you back from the battle! How blessed, how overjoyed she throws open her gates so that you may enter with gathered ranks, carrying trophies from the prostrate enemy!

With the triumphant men come women who, fighting the world, conquered even their own sex. Virgins come too, bearing the double glory of their warfare, and boys who surpassed their years through virtue. The rest of the multitude standing by follows your glory, treading in your footsteps with honors of praise that nearly join your own. The same sincerity of heart is in them, the same tenacity of faith. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by the traditions of the Gospel, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, or destined torments, or the loss of their estates, or bodily punishments. Days were set aside to test their faith. But the one who remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world; the one who hopes for eternity from God no longer calculates earthly time.

No one, my beloved brothers, no one should mutilate this glory, no one should weaken the uncorrupted firmness of those who stood firm with malicious detraction. When the day appointed for those who denied had passed, whoever had not professed within that day confessed himself a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord when he is seized by the hands of the Gentiles. The second step to glory is to be reserved for the Lord by a cautious withdrawal. The former is a public confession; the latter is a private one. The former conquers the judge of the world; the latter, content with God as his judge, guards a pure conscience with the integrity of his heart. There, fortitude is more prompt; here, solicitude is more secure. The former, with his hour approaching, was already found mature. The latter was perhaps delayed — he who abandoned his patrimony withdrew precisely because he was not going to deny; he certainly would have confessed if he had also been detained.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the distinction between public and private confessions and the specific circumstances of the two types of victors. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Locked Latin.
